correctness.rationale: The uniform proof classifies all A-fibers over selected B vertices, computes the critical mixed and pure four-vertex faces exactly, and invokes the proven acyclicity of sequential element matchings (Deshpande–Singh Proposition 2.10). It leaves one vertex plus \(n^2-3n-1\) three-cells for every integer \(n\ge4\), yielding an integral wedge by Forman theory. The standalone code checks distinct graph and modular-index predicates on every subset through n=8, directed Hasse acyclicity and exact critical sets through n=12, and mod-two homology \(n=4\)..8. These finite checks corroborate the analytic infinite proof.

value.rationale: Removing a canonical alternating Hamiltonian cycle from a complete bipartite graph is a natural spanning 2-factor deletion. The exact all-n integral homotopy classification of its first higher-independence complex changes the homology degree from one (undeleted graph) to three and gives quadratic nontrivial multiplicity \(n^2-3n-1\). It offers a structural reference case for topological effects of regular sparse edge deletion; the claim is not a routine corollary or arbitrary finite table.
